Let \(a=53^\circ\), \(b=81^\circ\), and \(c=x^\circ\). The equation is

\[
\tan a \tan b \tan c=\tan a+\tan b+\tan c.
\]

Rearrange:

\[
\tan c(\tan a\tan b-1)=\tan a+\tan b.
\]

Since \(\tan 53^\circ>1\) and \(\tan 81^\circ>1\), \(\tan 53^\circ\tan 81^\circ-1\neq 0\). Thus

\[
\tan c=\frac{\tan a+\tan b}{\tan a\tan b-1}.
\]

Using the tangent addition formula,

\[
\tan(a+b)=\frac{\tan a+\tan b}{1-\tan a\tan b},
\]

so

\[
\tan c=-\tan(a+b)=\tan(180^\circ-(a+b)).
\]

Now

\[
180^\circ-(53^\circ+81^\circ)=46^\circ.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\tan x^\circ=\tan 46^\circ.
\]

Since \(0<x<180\), we get

\[
x=46.
\]

\[
\boxed{46}
\]
